readme.text:
Read me first · redrawn from the ground up, 2026-11-05

The app is for people; the CLI is for machines. One binary is the CLI, the daemon and the app. One window: a pinned Library tab first, then a tab per open stack; no + tab, since the Library, ⌘O and a dropped folder are how a stack arrives.

Every screen names where it comes from in its frame title and its key strip. Every board uses the shop fixture's data, and the five palettes are the terminal's.

What is deliberately not here: a terminal pane (nothing to add over your own terminal), the timeline (P5, drawn when designed, not as a placeholder; the map is on page 2), Linux chrome (the same app; GNOME differs only in the window frame and tray).

flow_begin.text:
The lead-ins on this page

1 First launch → 2 Library, empty → (drop or ⌘O) → 3 a folder with no doze.hcl → pick a way → the stack's Overview.

4 Library with stacks is where the window opens from then on. Clicking a stopped stack → 5 its own Overview, every service down, each switch saying what Up starts → Up → the same page, waking.

doze open in a terminal lands on 4 with that stack's tab selected.

flow_daily.text:
On a row or tile: space is the switch (part of this run or not), p pins, ⏎ or a double click opens the service, l its logs, L all logs. The List view keeps the selected one in full beside the rows; Tiles and Map stay clean.

Off on one instance needs one new daemon verb (doze off web); everything else here is read from doze status as it is today.

flow_wrong.text:
Rule for every bad-news screen: the first line says what happened in plain words, the second says what doze is doing about it, and the buttons are the ways out. Nothing is hidden behind a log you have to go find.

A notification is sent once per episode, for a crash, a failed task, or a stuck wake; never for anything else.
